svg.text: The memory system — functional data in HBM, latency from a model

Nothing on this path is a DRAM: the “GPU memory” the kernel sees is the card's HBM behind a timing model that makes it look like whatever the +mm_ settings say. Determinism follows — congestion on the real HBM stalls target time instead of changing results.
Vortex (target time)
Cores → L1 → (L2/L3 if enabled)
the sockets' misses meet at the
cluster arbiter
VX_mem_to_axi
Tag buffer: UUID-wide upstream tags →
16 outstanding reads, 4-bit AXI id
(paired: PLATFORM_MEMORY_ID_WIDTH=4 ↔ idBits=4)
m_axi_mem_0 — one AXI4 port
512-bit data · 32-bit addr · INCR bursts
NUM_BANKS=1: the wrapper presents one port,
so Vortex builds one
FASED bridge (FireSim-generated)
Timing model — latency-bandwidth pipe
Runtime registers, set per run, no rebuild:
readLatency = 30 · writeLatency = 30 (target cycles)
readMaxReqs / writeMaxReqs ≤ maxReads/Writes = 16
Set via VORTEX_FIRESIM_ARGS plusargs:
+mm_readLatency_0=100 +mm_writeLatency_0=100
+mm_useHardwareDefaultRuntimeSettings_0 (covers the rest)
Functional model
Ingress/egress queues, per-id reorder buffer; reads and writes
go to host memory when accepted, responses are held until the
timing model's release cycle. Instrumented:
totalReads/Writes(Beats) · readMaxReqs · rrespError · …
printed by the driver on every stall report and watchdog
LoadMem widget — the host's side door
Kernel upload, buffer copy, readback: same host-memory master,
no target time passes. Chunk unit is 32-bit words.
Shell binding (per card, from its descriptor)
V80 (aved) — hw/syn/xilinx/platforms/v80.toml
host_mem_sp = "MEM" → HBM VNOC, 32 GB window
base = 0x40_0000_0000 (WithHostMemBase)
The whole 32-bit target map fits the window; the AFU
rebases every access. HBM0 (1 GB) would truncate it —
the stack sits just under 4 GB. HOST (QDMA slave
bridge) never completes reads: refused by the descriptor.
U55C (vitis)
HOST_MEM_SP = HBM[0:7] → 8 × 512 MB = 4 GiB
base = 0x0
A narrower binding silently serves only part of the map:
kernel uploads land outside it, reads return junk.
One host memory channel, 64-bit
Host-side AXI: beatBytes=8 at the host clock. This bounds
*simulation speed* under memory traffic, never target
timing: a starved FASED gates the target clock and FMR
rises; the kernel's cycle count is unchanged.
What the model does — and does not — capture
The default pipe is a flat-latency, fixed-parallelism abstraction. Its ceiling is easy to compute and easy to hit:
peak read bandwidth ≈ maxReads × 64 B / readLatency = 16 × 64 / 30 ≈ 34 B per target cycle — for the whole GPU
demo at 64 cores (memory-bound, IPC 0.18) and sgemm 1024³ (14.7 FLOP/cycle against ~2000 available) both sit on this ceiling. Raising it means
raising maxReads (compile time, area) or the modelled latencies (runtime), not a faster card.
There is no DRAM structure in the default model: no banks, rows, refresh, or contention. FASED has DDR3 FIFO/FR-FCFS models with those (compile-time
choice, WithDDR3FIFOMAS), and an optional tags-only LLC model; neither is enabled for Vortex today. HBM timing does not exist in FASED at all.
Configuration knobs, by where they live:
image build: FREQUENCY=60 STRATEGY=TIMING DEVICE=<part> HOST_MEM_SP=<tag> (hw/syn/firesim → platform build)
elaboration: NastiParameters(dataBits=512, addrBits=32, idBits=4) · BaseParams(maxReads/maxWrites=16) · platform toml [firesim]
per run: VORTEX_FIRESIM_ARGS="+mm_…_0=…" — the only knob that needs no rebuild
Address-width warning: the wrapper takes its AXI width from VX_CFG_MEM_ADDR_WIDTH (48 at XLEN=64) while the Scala side pins addrBits=32;
a disagreement is padded or truncated with no diagnostic. XLEN=64 on FireSim needs both sides changed together.
idBits is bounded both ways: 1<<idBits wraps Scala's Int at 32 (silently wrong responses); per-id state made idBits=8 cost 751K LUTs on a U55C. 4 matches what Vortex drives.
